reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the defect-mediated exchange-broadening mechanism from the second-order NiFeCoCrPdx system (P1, P4, P6, P7) to a first-order magnetostructural FeMnNiGeSi HEA, but the core idea—that defect density governs the shape and hysteresis of the magnetocaloric response—is already explicitly stated in those passages. The proposed intervention (mild annealing to reduce defects) and its predicted outcome (broadened transition, reduced hysteresis) are essentially the same as what was observed and explained in the earlier work, with only a change of material system and transition order. No new mechanistic insight or synthesis of conflicting evidence is offered.
